subject: BUG-268: updateStreak is LIVE in production and does not exist in the source tree
description:
Discovered 2026-09-07 when a functions deploy ABORTED: 'The following functions are found in your project but do not exist in your local source code: updateStreak(us-central1)'. Firebase refused to proceed rather than delete it in non-interactive mode, which is the correct behaviour and is the only reason anyone noticed. NOT DELETED, and must not be: we do not destroy, and this is a live Cloud Function whose callers and behaviour are unknown. WHY IT MATTERS TONIGHT SPECIFICALLY: it writes streak, one of the exact fields BUG-263 just removed from the client-writable allowlist and one of the inputs deriveXP consumes. All evening the assumption has been that syncProgress and recordProgress are the only two front doors to progress -- firestore.rules:132-138 now says so in a comment. This is a THIRD writer that nobody accounted for, running in production, invisible to grep because it is not in the repo. Its source is not in functions/ and therefore not in git, so nobody can review what it does, what it validates, or who calls it. INVESTIGATE BEFORE ANY FURTHER PROGRESS WORK: pull its deployed source (gcloud functions describe/download, or the Cloud Console), determine who calls it and what it writes, decide whether it is (a) dead and archivable, (b) live and needing its source restored to the repo, or (c) a forgery vector of the same class as recordProgress. Until then, treat 'syncProgress and recordProgress are the only writers' as UNPROVEN -- it is now known false. WORKAROUND USED TONIGHT so the BUG-264/266 patch could ship without touching it: deploy only the changed functions by name rather than the whole codebase, which skips the orphan check entirely. Never pass --force here; that would delete a live function to make a deploy quieter.
[2026-09-07 02:48] RESOLVED AND DOWNGRADED, investigated 2026-09-07 (not modified, not deleted). updateStreak is ACTIVE, last updated 2026-08-20T06:12:23Z per gcloud functions describe --gen2. ITS SOURCE WAS NEVER LOST: it matches functions/_archive/updateStreak-orphaned-2026-08-31.js exactly, confirmed by calling the live function and comparing behaviour -- so someone archived it correctly and the repo has it; only the deployed copy outlived the source tree. BEHAVIOUR, verified live on a throwaway account: first call returns {streak:1, alreadyUpdated:false} and sets lastLoginDate; an immediate second call the same day returns {streak:1, alreadyUpdated:true} and changes nothing. It increments by at most 1 per real calendar day per uid, gated on the SERVER's own Date.now() with no client-supplied date, and resets to 1 on a gap. An attacker calling it in a loop gains exactly nothing beyond what an honest daily visitor gains. It writes streak and lastLoginDate; nothing else reads lastLoginDate. CALLERS: ZERO. Grepped the live _app tree for callFunction('updateStreak' and httpsCallable(...,'updateStreak') -- no matches. Every text hit for the string in _app (jeopardy games, ModuleProgress.js) is an unrelated LOCAL js function that happens to share the name. SO IT IS NOT A FORGERY VECTOR and does not belong on the BUG-264 list: it is a dead-but-live function with no caller and a self-limiting write. My earlier framing ('a third writer nobody accounted for', 'treat only-two-writers as known false') OVERSTATED it -- the claim that only syncProgress and recordProgress write progress is still true for every path a client can actually reach. Remaining action is housekeeping, not security: decide whether to redeploy it from the archive so source and production agree, or retire it properly. Until one of those, every full 'firebase deploy --only functions' will keep aborting on the orphan check, which is how it was found and is not a bad outcome.
